subject: Cross-region availability incidents — request for geo-failover SLA and credit proposal
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex@corefin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah@corefin.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T16:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Service interruptions in EU — cross-region availability concerns

Hi Soojin,

Quick note from CoreFin ops — over the past two weeks we saw two separate windows where requests routed to the EU cluster experienced 10-30s tail latency and a partial regional outage for ~18 minutes on 2026-09-24. Impact: delayed user-facing workflows and queued jobs in our ingestion pipeline. I attached our incident timeline (corefin_incident_timeline.pdf).

We need to understand:
- What caused the regional degradation and why automatic failover didn't protect us?
- Can Redwood commit to a geo-failover SLA / a regional availability guarantee (we were expecting 99.99 regional)?
- If not, what commercial remediation (credits / short-term compensation) can you provide while we evaluate a longer-term mitigation?

Procurement is already asking for a concrete remediation plan because this will affect our renewal. Can you loop in engineering and legal?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Reliability, CoreFin
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@corefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah@corefin.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T10:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Service interruptions in EU — cross-region availability concerns

Alex — thanks for the timeline and level set. I’m sorry for the disruption; fully appreciate why this is urgent for your renewal discussion. Quick summary of next steps from our side:

1) Immediate mitigation: we’ll enable a temporary cross-region routing policy for CoreFin tonight (read: route new traffic to our US replica when EU latency spikes exceed thresholds) and increase probe frequency on the EU pool.
2) Credit offer: as an interim gesture we can provide a one-time operational credit equivalent to 10% of your September invoice while we investigate root cause.
3) Longer-term: we want to present a formal uplift proposal — Dedicated pool + geo-replicated failover with an SLA addendum (p50/p95/p99 latency commitments and regional availability target). Marissa is drafting the commercial amendment and Priyom will scope the technical design.

Can you confirm whether your legal/procurement would accept a short SOW + addendum (DocuSign) with a pilot commitment? If yes, we’ll put a draft in your inbox by Monday.

— Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex@corefin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah@corefin.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Service interruptions in EU — cross-region availability concerns

Soojin — thank you. A few clarifying questions from our side before we schedule legal review:

• Can Redwood commit to an automated failover time objective? Our tolerance is failover within 60s for control-plane-triggered routing and <2s for data-plane cutover once failover is initiated.
• The interim credit — is that bill credit or service credit, and how will it be applied?
• For the Dedicated + geo-replica pilot: we need a two-week smoke period and then a 3-month pilot; after pilot we’d like the option to convert to a longer reserved commitment if results meet SLOs.

If you can include the above items in the draft SOW and mark technical owners, we’ll pull legal in. Also add a pointer to any runbooks or observability hooks we can use during the pilot.

Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@corefin.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah@corefin.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Service interruptions in EU — cross-region availability concerns

Alex — thanks for the specifics, very helpful. I’ve pulled together a formal proposal we can put into a short SOW + addendum (attached: draft_geo_sow.pdf). High-level commercial and technical commitments we’re offering:

Commercial offer:
- One-time bill credit: 10% of Sept invoice applied as credit on next invoice (applies immediately once agreement signed).
- Pilot pricing: 3-month Dedicated + geo-replicated failover at pilot rates; option to convert to a 12-month reserved contract with a 10% uplift on pilot price.

Operational & SLA commitments:
- Failover objectives: we will commit to an automated routing decision within 60s of an outage condition and aim for data-plane cutover <3s once routing is activated. We’ll include exact detection thresholds in the addendum.
- Availability target during converted reserved term: 99.99% regional availability (measured monthly), backed by service credits as defined in the addendum.
- Observability & runbooks: full read-only access to the RedBox runbook for your SREs during the pilot + tokenized tracing hooks and per-route latency dashboards.

Next steps / timeline:
1) I’ll send the SOW and an addendum for legal review (DocuSign link included in related_links).
2) Proposed mutual action plan: pilot kick-off within 7 business days of signed SOW; two-week smoke then 3-month pilot.
3) Owners: Priyom will lead the tech design and implementation; Soojin will manage commercial/exec updates.

If that sounds reasonable, please confirm and we’ll route the DocuSign. We requested decision by 2026-10-11 to meet your renewal cadence.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
(attachment: draft_geo_sow.pdf)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@corefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah@corefin.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Service interruptions in EU — cross-region availability concerns

Alex — following up to confirm we’ve routed the draft SOW and addendum (see attachments/DocuSign). Priyom is available for a 30-min technical deep dive Tuesday or Wednesday next week to walk the runbook, failover detection thresholds, and what observability we’ll make available during the pilot.

Quick recap of asks we’ll cover on the call:
- Confirm failover detection thresholds and expected failover timelines.
- Walk the smoke test checklist for the two-week period.
- Review what success metrics trigger conversion to reserved commitment.

Please let me know preferred time slots and whether your procurement wants any edits to the credit application language (bill credit vs. account-level credit). Appreciate the quick turnaround here — we want to make sure CoreFin has a stable path forward for renewal.

— Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
